newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Swedbank boosts earnings, shares rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Swedbank boosts earnings, shares rise.

text.p: Swedbank posted a nine percent rise in operating profit to 1.32 billion crowns ($172.7 million) on Wednesday, the second Swedish bank to report better first quarter earnings.
Profits were helped by higher net commission, lower costs and reduced loan losses.

"Substantially higher commission income from, among other things, fund and insurance savings, compensated for the decrease in net income from financial operations and expenses have decreased," said chief executive Reinhold Geijer.
The figures cheered market players and Swedbank's shares jumped to trade at 142.5 crowns by midafternoon, up 4-1/2.
"The report seems to be in line," Keith Baird, analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, told Reuters.
"There are some worries about the sustainability of profits in banks so if a bank can reach the same earnings level or better, the market will be relieved."
Swedbank's report followed first quarter figures from rival Handelsbanken on Monday which showed operating profit after loan losses rose 14 percent to 1.73 billion crowns.
Analysts were glad both posted a rise in net commission. Swedbank showed a 33 percent rise to 792 million crowns while Handelsbanken had an 18 percent increase to 797 million.
"We are positive on higher commissions as we see that as the banks' future growth market," said Jesper Brydensholt, analyst at Aros Securities.
Swedbank cut costs to 2.12 billion crowns from 2.19 billion and loan losses declined to 300 million crowns from 460 million crowns for a loan loss ratio fall to 0.3 percent from 0.5.
Swedbank's lending and savings rose and earnings per share increased to 3.36 crowns from 3.10.
Its capital adequacy ratio was 12.4 percent at the end of the first quarter, compared to 11.8 percent a year earlier.
Net interest income was little changed at 2.41 billion crowns compared to 2.40 billion, despite the government charge for deposit guarantee doubling to 113 million crowns.
Handelsbanken's net interest income was also burdened by a doubling of the deposit guarantee to 75 million crowns but still rose 17 percent to 2.61 billion crowns.
"It looks to me as if Handelsbanken is doing better than Swedbank when looking at growth and margins," Baird said. "Swedbank's underlying situation does not seem to be as good as it could be."

Swedbank noted that total income fell three percent to 3.73 billion crowns following lower net income from financial operations after a decline in long-term interest rates boosted 1996 figures. Net income from financial operations dropped to 117 million crowns from 479 million.
But Brydensholt saw Swedbank as well positioned with its large mortgage lending unit Robur as he expected most loan growth in the mortgage business.
